fieldMarks: One of the largest salamanders: long cylindrical body to about 117 cm with four vestigial legs, each foot with three toes; hind legs shorter than front.
Dark brown to black above with a markedly lighter belly and a dark underside to the neck.
Lidless, reduced eyes; retains a laterally compressed tail and lateral-line system as an adult; copious mucus makes it hard to grip; males have wider, heavier heads.
behavior: Nocturnal, most active around midnight; ambush predator that eats mainly crayfish, plus fish, insects, snails and amphibians.
Non-migratory with a small home range around a burrow; aestivates in burrows in dry seasons; individuals often show bite marks.
Active throughout the year along the Gulf Coast.
habitat: Wooded alluvial swamps, calcareous streams, floodland marshes and lakes, seepy pools and bayou or cypress-slough banks with extensive crayfish burrow networks.
range: NatureServe lists it in the central and lower Mississippi valley region: Missouri, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama.

lookalikes.name: Two-toed amphiuma
lookalikes.howToTell: Two-toed has two toes on each foot (three-toed has three); both occur in Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama.
